input.hypothesis: The US extends semiconductor export controls to legacy nodes

nodes.statement: US extends semiconductor export controls to legacy nodes (e.g., 28nm and above) within 180 days
nodes.resolution: BIS issues new rulemaking or amendment to EAR expanding Entity List or license requirements to legacy process technologies
nodes.rationale: Escalating US-China tech tensions and national security concerns over legacy chip supply chains increase likelihood of broader controls.
assumptions: BIS prioritizes legacy nodes in next rulemaking cycle
Congressional support remains for expanded controls
No major diplomatic breakthrough with China

nodes.statement: BIS initiates Advanced Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (ANPRM) on legacy node controls
nodes.resolution: Federal Register publishes ANPRM seeking public comment on extending controls to 28nm+ chips
nodes.rationale: ANPRM is standard first step for major regulatory changes; aligns with typical 6-12 month implementation timeline.
assumptions: BIS has completed internal policy review

nodes.statement: Major semiconductor equipment suppliers announce supply chain decoupling from Chinese foundries
nodes.resolution: ASML, Applied Materials, Lam Research publicly disclose cessation of shipments to SMIC, Hua Hong, and other Chinese foundries for legacy nodes
nodes.rationale: Equipment suppliers typically comply preemptively with export control expansions to avoid penalties.
analogs: 2023 Applied Materials divestiture of Chinese JV
assumptions: Chinese foundries lack alternative equipment sources

nodes.statement: Chinese foundries report significant wafer capacity utilization decline
nodes.resolution: SMIC, Hua Hong report >20% sequential drop in utilization rates for 28nm and above processes
nodes.rationale: Legacy node foundries heavily dependent on US-origin equipment and materials; supply chain disruption leads to production delays.
assumptions: Chinese foundries cannot rapidly source non-US alternatives

nodes.statement: Global legacy node wafer pricing declines by >15%
nodes.resolution: Spot market prices for 28nm+ wafers fall below $4,500 per wafer from current ~$5,300
nodes.rationale: Oversupply from reduced Chinese demand and inventory correction drives price declines across legacy nodes.
assumptions: Chinese demand accounts for >25% of global legacy wafer consumption

nodes.statement: Semiconductor equipment stocks decline >10% on expanded export control fears
nodes.resolution: SOXX index drops below 140 from current ~155 due to reduced addressable market
nodes.rationale: Equipment suppliers face revenue headwinds from restricted Chinese market access and order cancellations.
analogs: 2022 ASML stock drop on China restrictions
assumptions: Chinese market represents >20% of equipment revenue

nodes.statement: US semiconductor manufacturing stocks decline on reduced global demand outlook
nodes.resolution: MU, AMD, INTC stocks drop >15% as legacy node oversupply impacts pricing and volumes
nodes.rationale: Memory and logic chipmakers face margin pressure from legacy node oversupply and pricing declines.
assumptions: Legacy node oversupply affects entire semiconductor ecosystem

nodes.name: SMH ETF Price
nodes.rationale: Market prices in semiconductor export control expansion and its impact on legacy node demand.
assumptions: SMH holds significant exposure to legacy node companies
Market reacts within 30 days of policy announcement

nodes.name: Global 28nm Wafer Price
nodes.rationale: Legacy node wafer pricing directly impacted by Chinese foundry demand reduction and supply chain disruption.
assumptions: Chinese foundries account for 30% of 28nm demand
Alternative buyers cannot absorb excess supply

nodes.name: SOXX Equipment Index
nodes.rationale: Equipment sector faces revenue headwinds from restricted Chinese market access.
assumptions: US equipment suppliers derive 25% revenue from China

nodes.name: SMIC Utilization Rate
nodes.rationale: Chinese foundry utilization directly impacted by equipment and material supply chain restrictions.

assumptions: Chinese foundries lack alternative equipment sources

edges.mechanism: Equipment sector weakness signals broader semiconductor downturn
assumptions: Equipment stocks lead semiconductor sector performance

assumptions: SMH accurately prices in export control expansion

assumptions: Alternative applications cannot absorb excess supply

edges.mechanism: Equipment index decline validates sector headwinds

summary.headline: US export control expansion to legacy nodes could trigger 15-20% decline in SMH within 180 days via supply chain disruption and demand destruction
summary.mainUncertainty: Timing and scope of BIS rulemaking, and whether Chinese foundries can source non-US alternatives
followUps: Monitor Federal Register for ANPRM on legacy nodes
Track SMIC and Hua Hong utilization rates
Watch SOXX equipment index for sector repricing
